claim.quote: Here we present the first observation of strangeness enhancement in high-multiplicity pp collisions.

key_value_text.quote: We find that the integrated yields of strange and multi-strange particles relative to pions increases significantly with the event charged-particle multiplicity... In high-multiplicity events strangeness production reaches values similar to those observed in Pb-Pb collisions, where a QGP is formed.
key_value_text.value: Integrated yields of strange and multi-strange particles relative to pions increase significantly with event charged-particle multiplicity, reaching values similar to those seen in Pb-Pb collisions at the highest pp multiplicities.

name: First observation of strangeness enhancement in high-multiplicity pp collisions

summary.plain: ALICE found that the busier a proton-proton collision, the more strange particles it produces relative to pions, up to values similar to those in lead-lead collisions, where a quark-gluon plasma is formed. The paper presents this as the first observation of strangeness enhancement in high-multiplicity pp collisions.
summary.technical: ALICE measurement (pp at √s = 7 TeV) of strange (K0S, Lambda) and multi-strange (Xi, Omega) hadron yields relative to pions as a function of charged-particle multiplicity. The collaboration presents 'the first observation of strangeness enhancement in high-multiplicity pp collisions': the yields relative to pions increase significantly with multiplicity and, at the highest multiplicities, reach values similar to those observed in Pb-Pb collisions.

title: Enhanced production of multi-strange hadrons in high-multiplicity proton-proton collisions
why_it_matters: Strangeness enhancement was originally proposed as a signature of QGP formation in nuclear collisions, where it is more pronounced for multi-strange baryons. The paper reports it in high-multiplicity pp collisions and says the agreement with p-Pb results indicates that the phenomenon is related to the final system created in the collision.
